sources.page: the top frame's page: any site the user visits
sources.frame: any frame, including cross-origin and sandboxed iframes
sources.main-world: a value returned from script evaluated in the page's main world, which the page can rewrite (Chromium evaluates there; WebKit uses an isolated world)
sources.sync: a record from another device that holds the sync key
sources.other-app: another app on this Mac, through an opened URL, an Apple Event or a notification
sources.plugin: an approved plugin, within its manifest's permissions
sources.socket: a same-user process on the control socket while Settings > Advanced > Let programs control Ardia is on
sources.native: the browser's own native layer, relaying OS input
sources.import: a file or browser profile the user chose to import

customEvents.ardia:media-element: Page-world shim names a media element for the isolated world to track; only an HTMLMediaElement is taken, and only its own playback state is read
customEvents.ardia:media-fault: Page-world shim relays a media error on the listed media sites only; a string of at most 64 characters, at most 200 per page, classified natively by WebKitMediaFaults.event
customEvents.ardia:media-session: Page-world shim relays the page's own Media Session: actions filtered to a fixed list, positions must be finite numbers; it describes only the page's own media
customEvents.ardia:app-badge: Page-world shim relays the Badging API from the top frame; native requires the main frame and takes the origin from frameInfo, as for the badge API itself
customEvents.ardia:media-action: Dispatched by the isolated world into the page world to run a media action on the page's own elements. A page that dispatches its own only acts on itself
customEvents.ardia:notification-reply: Sent by the isolated world to WebKit's page-world Notification shim. A page that dispatches its own only misleads its own shim; it carries nothing from other origins
customEvents.ardia:notification: WebKit's page-world Notification shim posts it to the isolated world. Any page script can send the same; native ignores the claimed origin and requires the main frame, frameInfo.securityOrigin equal to the top origin and the site's permission set to allow (WebKitTab+Site.swift)
